state:
user: the postgres connection pool keeps exhausting under load
assistant: Root cause: pgbouncer pool_mode was session, not transaction. Switched to transaction mode and set max_client_conn=500; exhaustion stopped. Verified under a load test.

user: CI is flaky, date tests pass locally but fail on the runner
assistant: Runner is UTC and tests assumed local TZ. Pinned TZ=UTC in CI and froze the clock with a fixture. Green across 20 runs.

user: worker memory climbs until OOM after a few hours
assistant: asyncio tasks made with create_task were never awaited/cancelled, so refs and exceptions piled up. Added a task registry that cancels on shutdown plus a done-callback. RSS flat over 12h.

user: browser calls fail with CORS but curl works
assistant: The reverse proxy dropped OPTIONS so preflight never hit the CORS middleware. Added an OPTIONS passthrough in nginx returning 204 with ACAO headers. Fixed.

user: intermittent deadlock in the ingest pipeline
assistant: Two goroutines took locks A,B in opposite orders. Enforced a global lock-ordering (always A before B) and added a lint check. No deadlock in 100k runs.

user: prod image crashes with a glibc symbol error, builds fine locally
assistant: A transitive dep shipped a wheel built against a newer glibc than the slim base image. Pinned the base to bookworm and rebuilt the wheel from source in CI. Crash gone.

user: invoice totals are off by a cent sometimes
assistant: Float accumulation over line items. Switched all money to integer cents and only formatted to decimal at the edge. Reconciliation now exact.

user: review the webhook fetcher
assistant: It fetched arbitrary user-supplied URLs server-side — SSRF to internal metadata endpoints. Added an allowlist of schemes/hosts and blocked link-local ranges. Confirmed 169.254.x is now refused.

user: users randomly get logged out
assistant: Traced it to two app instances signing JWTs with different secrets after a rolling deploy — a request hitting the other instance fails verification. I haven't fixed it yet, but the fix is to share one signing key via the secret store. Diagnosis confirmed by correlating logout spikes with deploys.

user: the search endpoint is slow
assistant: First assumed a missing index — added one, no change. Real cause was N+1: each result refetched its author. Batched with a single IN query; p95 dropped 1200ms->90ms. (The index was a dead end — the slowness was never the DB scan.)

user: uploads over 5MB fail with the SDK
assistant: Known bug in sdk v3.2 multipart (github.com/x/y/issues/912). Worked around it by setting forcePathStyle=true and chunking at 4MB until they release the fix. Uploads succeed now; leave a TODO to drop the workaround after v3.3.

user: should we use a queue or cron for the digest job?
assistant: Went with cron+advisory-lock over a queue: volume is ~1/day, a queue adds infra we'd have to run, and the advisory lock prevents double-fire across instances. Documented the tradeoff; revisit if cadence goes sub-minute.

user: the crawler keeps getting 429s
assistant: The API has an undocumented 600 req/min ceiling and returns Retry-After only sometimes. Settled on token-bucket at 8 req/s with jitter + honoring Retry-After when present. Zero 429s over an hour.

user: TF_CPP settings aren't taking effect
assistant: The env var must be set BEFORE the module is imported; setting it after import is silently ignored because the value is read at import time. Moved the os.environ set above the import. Gotcha worth remembering for any import-time-config lib.

user: what does git rebase do?
assistant: git rebase moves your commits onto a new base commit, rewriting history into a linear sequence instead of a merge commit.

user: how does quicksort work?
assistant: Pick a pivot, partition elements into less/greater, recurse on each side; average O(n log n), worst O(n^2) on already-sorted input without a good pivot.

user: dashboard takes 6s to load
assistant: [profiled, read ORM logs...] The serializer triggered a query per row for permissions — 400 rows = 400 queries. Prefetched permissions in one query and memoized per request; load time 6s->380ms.

user: el cron no dispara en producción pero sí en local
assistant: The prod container runs UTC and the cron expression assumed local time (UTC-5), so it fired at the wrong hour and looked dead during the window checked. Converted the schedule to UTC and documented it. Confirmed it now fires on time.
